Re: Appeal of prior-authorization denial  
Requested service: Total knee replacement  
CPT: 27447  
Reference number: POC-5585B8DEE7-94152  
Date of denial notice: August 12, 2026

Dear Oscar Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my total knee replacement, CPT 27447. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I request reconsideration based on the enclosed clinical records and the medical-necessity criteria in Oscar Clinical Guideline: Total Knee Arthroplasty (Replacement), CG069, Version 6.

The guideline states:

“Total knee arthroplasty for a unilateral knee is considered medically necessary when ONE of the following criteria are met.”

For advanced joint disease, the guideline requires:

“The member meets medical necessity for advanced joint disease as indicated by ALL of the following:”

“Radiologic or arthroscopic findings of advanced knee joint destruction documented by the treating surgeon and/or radiologist for ONE of the following: i. Kellgren Lawrence Grade IV radiographic findings…”

The July 1, 2026 weight-bearing radiographs document bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments, lateral joint-space narrowing, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis. These findings satisfy the guideline’s advanced-joint-disease requirement.

The guideline also requires:

“Severe pain persisting in the affected knee that interferes with functional activity or age-appropriate activities for at least 3-months…”

I have had 9 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest. The pain prevents me from climbing stairs without assistance and wakes me three to four times each night. The orthopedic examination documents varus alignment, crepitus, effusion, and restricted range of motion from 5 to 100 degrees. These records establish persistent, functionally limiting pain.

The guideline further requires:

“There has been a failure to decrease pain or improve function after at least a 3-month trial of conservative treatment (non-surgical)…”

The submitted records document the following conservative treatment:

- NSAID treatment for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, including 18 visits from May 7, 2026, through July 16, 2026, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- A corticosteroid injection on June 8, 2026, which produced only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- Continued progressive symptoms and substantial functional impairment despite these treatments.

The guideline identifies conservative treatment components including:

“Active and ongoing participation in a physical therapy (documented) or a well documented home exercise program under the supervision of a physical therapist or physician…”

and

“Oral/topical medications (e.g., analgesics, NSAIDs, serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake Inhibitor (duloxetine)), unless poorly tolerated or contraindicated…”

The physical therapy records and medication history address these requirements. The limited, temporary response to the corticosteroid injection further documents failure of non-surgical treatment.

The records also document that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. Nothing in the submitted records identifies a contraindication to surgery. The requested procedure is CPT 27447, the total knee arthroplasty procedure addressed by the Oscar guideline.

The guideline also states:

“No contraindication present or the request is not considered Experimental or Investigational, or Not Medically Necessary based on the indications listed below…”

There is no active infection, untreated wound or skin infection, severe obesity, or other documented contraindication in the clinical summary. The requested procedure is a standard total knee replacement for documented grade 4, bone-on-bone knee disease, not a customized or experimental implant request.

The corticosteroid injection occurred on June 8, 2026. The guideline states:

“No intra-articular steroid injections to the knee within three months before the surgery date…”

Accordingly, please confirm that the surgery is scheduled on or after September 8, 2026, or advise whether any additional documentation is required regarding this timing requirement. If Oscar considers the conservative-treatment documentation incomplete because the supervised therapy period was 10 weeks rather than a full 3 months, please identify that specific deficiency and allow the treating surgeon to provide any required supplemental documentation, including documentation of the continued home exercise or conservative-treatment program.

Please reverse the denial and approve the requested total knee replacement. If Oscar continues to deny the request, please provide the specific missing records, the exact criterion that Oscar finds unmet, and the complete clinical review materials used in reaching the decision, including any delegated vendor criteria applied to this request.

Please send the appeal determination to me and to my treating surgeon, Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery.

Sincerely,

Morgan Brooks
